title: - Bhikkhus, when the great ocean swells, the great rivers swell; when the great rivers swell, the small rivers swell; when the small rivers swell,…
content: - Bhikkhus, when the great ocean swells, the great rivers swell; when the great rivers swell, the small rivers swell; when the small rivers swell, the large lakes swell; when the large lakes swell, the small lakes swell. So too, bhikkhus, when ignorance swells, formations swell; when formations swell, consciousness swells; when consciousness swells, name-and-form swells; when name-and-form swells, the six sense bases swell; when the six sense bases swell, contact swells; when contact swells, feeling swells; when feeling swells, craving swells; when craving swells, clinging swells; when clinging swells, existence swells; when existence swells, birth swells; when birth swells, aging and death swell.

title: Bhikkhus, just as a man takes a hot pot from a potter's kiln and places it on level ground to cool, and the broken pieces…
content: Bhikkhus, just as a man takes a hot pot from a potter's kiln and places it on level ground to cool, and the broken pieces are swept aside. So too, bhikkhus, when he feels a feeling ending with the body, he understands: 'I feel a feeling ending with the body.' When he feels a feeling ending with life, he understands: 'I feel a feeling ending with life.' He understands: 'With the breakup of the body after death, all feelings that are not delighted in will become cool, the body will be left aside.'

title: Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Thoughts of renunciation, thoughts of non-ill-will, thoughts of harmlessness — these, carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.
content: Carpenter, what are wholesome thoughts? Thoughts of renunciation, thoughts of non-ill-will, thoughts of harmlessness — these, carpenter, are called wholesome thoughts.

title: Bhikkhus, 'This Dhamma is for one who is concentrated, this Dhamma is not for one who is unconcentrated' — thus it has been said. For…
content:
Bhikkhus, 'This Dhamma is for one who is concentrated, this Dhamma is not for one who is unconcentrated' — thus it has been said. For what reason is it said?
Bhikkhus, here, a bhikkhu, secluded from sensual pleasures, secluded from unwholesome states... enters and abides in the fourth jhāna. Bhikkhus, 'This Dhamma is for one who is concentrated, this Dhamma is not for one who is unconcentrated' — thus it has been said, and for this reason it was said.

title: Bhikkhus, here you should train thus: 'We will keep our minds undefiled, we will not utter harsh speech, we will dwell compassionate, with a mind…
content: Bhikkhus, here you should train thus: 'We will keep our minds undefiled, we will not utter harsh speech, we will dwell compassionate, with a mind of loving-kindness, without inner hatred. We will dwell pervading that person with a mind imbued with loving-kindness. And with that person as a basis, we will dwell pervading the entire world with a mind imbued with loving-kindness, vast, immeasurable, without hostility, without ill-will.' Bhikkhus, you should train thus.

title: Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the summer, when all the grain has been gathered into the barn, a cowherd, tending the cows, sitting…
content:
Bhikkhus, just as at the end of the summer, when all the grain has been gathered into the barn, a cowherd, tending the cows, sitting at the root of a tree or in the open, might think about what needs to be done, and thinks: 'These are the cows.' So too, bhikkhus, there was what needed to be done, and I thought: 'These are the states.'
Bhikkhus, I exerted myself, was energetic, not passive, mindfulness was established without confusion, my body was tranquil, without agitation, my mind was concentrated and unified.

title: Just as, sisters, there is a great tree standing with heartwood, with roots that are impermanent, subject to change; with a trunk that is impermanent,…
content: Just as, sisters, there is a great tree standing with heartwood, with roots that are impermanent, subject to change; with a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; with branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; with its shadow that is impermanent, subject to change. If someone were to say: 'This great tree standing with heartwood has roots that are impermanent, subject to change; a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; but its shadow is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change' — would that person be speaking correctly?" "No, venerable sir." "Why is that?" "Venerable sir, this great tree has roots that are impermanent, subject to change; a trunk that is impermanent, subject to change; branches and leaves that are impermanent, subject to change; let alone its shadow — that too is impermanent, subject to change!" "That is correct, sisters! If someone were to say: 'These six internal bases are impermanent, and the feeling — pleasant, painful, or neither-painful-nor-pleasant — that arises dependent on these six internal bases is permanent, everlasting, eternal, not subject to change' — would that person be speaking correctly?" "No, venerable sir." "Why is that?" "Venerable sir, dependent on this and that condition, this and that feeling arises. With the cessation of those conditions, those feelings cease and pass away." "Good, good, sisters! That is indeed the true perception of a noble disciple with right wisdom.

title: - Bhikkhus, form is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form,…
content: - Bhikkhus, form is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past form, does not delight in future form, and for present form practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation. Bhikkhus, feeling is impermanent ... perception is impermanent ... formations are impermanent ... Bhikkhus, consciousness is impermanent, past and future, let alone the present. Seeing this, bhikkhus, a learned noble disciple has no regret for past consciousness, does not delight in future consciousness, and for present consciousness practices for disenchantment, dispassion, and cessation.

title: Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and thinks of going forth from home to homelessness,…
content:
Bhikkhus, when a noble disciple shaves off his hair and beard, puts on the yellow robe, and thinks of going forth from home to homelessness, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple intends to do battle with Māra!' This, bhikkhus, is the first divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, when a noble disciple dwells devoted to developing the seven factors of enlightenment, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple does battle with Māra!' This, bhikkhus, is the second divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

Furthermore, bhikkhus, when a noble disciple, by the destruction of the taints, in this very life, with direct knowledge, realizes, attains, and abides in the taintless liberation of mind and liberation by wisdom, at that moment, bhikkhus, a divine shout arises among the devas: 'This noble disciple has won the battle! Standing at the head of the battle, having been victorious, he dwells.' This, bhikkhus, is the third divine shout that arises from time to time among the devas.

title: Who is infatuated with women, with drink, with gambling, And squanders all he has — that is the cause of downfall. Who is not content…
content:
Who is infatuated with women, with drink, with gambling,
And squanders all he has — that is the cause of downfall.

Who is not content with his own wife, and is seen with prostitutes or others' wives —
That is the cause of downfall.

Who, having passed youth, takes a young, still-breasted wife
And cannot sleep from jealousy — that is the cause of downfall.
